body:
## Direction

**Direction A—Git-native commit transactions—is active.** A general Git-backed Directory representation (B) is deferred; engine-owned object storage (C) is a separate future design. This remains a draft, not a claim of production readiness or crash durability.

Start with the [design and continuation guide](https://github.com/vito/dagger/blob/fix-agent-git-history-no-fetch/internal-docs/git-native-workspace-commits.md) for implementation details, reproducible tests, and next steps. Continue from the PR's current head on `vito/dagger:fix-agent-git-history-no-fetch`.

## Summary

Draft implementation of native Git transactions and incremental source materialization for agent workspace commits. No new public GraphQL API; internal schema helpers and persistence metadata are added.

- **Native commit construction:** stage selected paths through a private index over cached objects, write trees/commits directly, and store only new objects in a COW child. No retained checkout or history copy for supported same-base local commits.
- **Native workspace reconciliation:** use cached trees and explicit-base Git merging, then replay changed-path checkout transitions. Preserve legacy checkout-skip behavior for raw bytes and filesystem metadata instead of returning an apparently identical raw Directory.
- **Incremental source checkout:** retain exact local parent provenance as an owned, persisted dependency; update a canonical parent checkout through COW rather than rematerializing the whole repository. Dirty source worktrees are never the baseline. Complex controls/submodules and retained `.git` checkouts use the existing path.
- **Safety and compatibility:** preserve approval/identity boundaries, explicit inputs and generic fallbacks; use read-only object mounts and rooted filesystem operations; propagate real failures and release abandoned snapshots. Reftable storage explicitly falls back because native publication writes loose refs. Native storage intentionally retains unrelated source refs/tags—an explicit review point.

The branch also retains the supporting local-history/source-checkout no-fetch work, bounded remote-log fetching from #14168, and nested interactive CLI attachable fixes needed for snapshot approval.

## Motivation

Small workspace commits were repeatedly reconstructing filesystem checkouts and fetching already-cached history, while the actual Git commit subprocess was comparatively cheap. The original agent trace and detailed investigation are recorded in the continuation guide; they are not a controlled before/after benchmark.

## Current measurements

Deterministic packed local fixture: **12,002 files, ~98 MB**, three sequential one-file scoped commits per run, with an unselected edit preserved. The harness measures status, commit, history, tree consumption and the next edit separately. Build/capture and LLM latency are not commit timing.

| Checkpoint | Median `Workspace.withCommit` | Median full measured cycle |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pre-native baseline | 11.07s | 11.77s |
| Native commit construction | 4.59s | 5.38s |
| Native reconciliation | 2.28s | 3.04s |
| Incremental source checkout | **0.74s** | **1.93s** |

The final row aggregates two runs/six commits: commit range **0.56–1.66s**, cycle range **1.47–2.45s**. Earlier rows use three observations each. A subsequent three-commit validation run measured a **0.738s commit median / 1.638s full-cycle median** (ranges **0.613–0.749s / 1.539–2.285s**); it is not folded into the table.

Telemetry verifies actual native execution, with **no general merge reconstructions, commit-time fetches, or full source checkouts inside ordinary benchmark commits**. Initial capture still fetches, and cold canonical parents can require materialization.

**These are synthetic-fixture measurements, not benchmarks of committing in `dagger/dagger` or a fresh interactive-agent workflow.** Runs used separate engines and are not controlled universal speedup ratios or tail-percentile estimates. Full cycles remain above one second. Outliers and measurement details are in the guide; new loose-object bytes must not be confused with physical storage allocation.

## Coverage and validation

- Full `core`/`core/schema` race tests, targeted from-source engine oracles, and CI-matching root-module lint pass locally. The known lint violations were fixed; other inspected remote failures showed transport/session errors and still require reruns before claiming green CI.
- Coverage checks commit identity and parentage, scoped/pending edits, rich filesystem metadata, fallbacks, cleanup, and checkout equivalence. A **56-commit sequential/concurrent history test** verifies object integrity, source isolation, and actual native/incremental execution—not just eligibility. Provenance dependencies are retained across two cache restarts.
- Engine tests use explicit private sessions to avoid inherited SDK session variables accidentally selecting the wrong engine. These checks do not establish engine crash durability or replace restart/GC stress testing.

## Remaining work

1. Benchmark scoped commits and full edit/review/commit loops in the actual `dagger/dagger` repository; run a fresh interactive-agent smoke test against verified from-source binaries.
2. Validate graceful restart/eviction, GC ownership, longer-lived storage growth, and physical allocation. Existing cache persistence remains best-effort, not a crash-durable Git database.
3. Review eligibility/fallback boundaries and intentional ref/tag retention, and rerun remote CI. Continue Direction A only where measurements justify it; status/diff preparation and checkpoint/overlay composition remain candidates.

See the [continuation priorities](https://github.com/vito/dagger/blob/fix-agent-git-history-no-fetch/internal-docs/git-native-workspace-commits.md#continuation-priorities) for the detailed handoff.
